tldr: Four items share a "Same X, Different Y" title pattern, not one event. Three arXiv papers (Oct 22-26) cover chemistry identifier binding, credit assignment for agentic RL, and cross-outlet news framing.
whats_new: A Nov 1 Hacker News post reports a 17-point gap between agents running the same model across 21 MCP servers, the only item here about agent engineering.
why_it_matters: The title match is a coincidence, but the MCP post carries the usable lesson: the agent harness, not just the model, can swing results, so evaluate the full stack.

beats.headline: Two arXiv papers on reliability and agentic RL
beats.summary: Identifier binding failures in chemistry LLMs, and twin-world credit assignment for agentic reinforcement learning.

beats.headline: A multi-agent system compares news framing across outlets
beats.summary: A research prototype aimed at news analysis, loosely related to the rest.

beats.headline: Same model, different agent: 17 points apart on 21 MCP servers
beats.summary: A practitioner post on agent-level variance with a fixed model.

open_questions: Does the MCP post publish its harness differences, prompts and scoring method so the 17-point gap can be reproduced?
Do any of the arXiv papers release code or evals that apply to tool-using agents?
take_for_builders: When comparing agents, hold the model fixed and vary the harness in your own eval on your MCP servers; treat the 17-point figure as one unverified blog result until reproduced.
